# Pitch numbers (generated by scripts/pitch_numbers.py; do not edit by hand)

Every number comes from web/public/data, the same files the app loads: hourly samples, the centre of the Sun or Earth above the terrain horizon, observer 2 m above the ground. Checks against JPL and NASA: docs/VALIDATION.md.

## 4. When can a 14-day mission land at Malapert Massif (mma01)?

Mission: 336 h on the surface, at least 70 % sunlit, at least 50 % Earth visible, no darkness longer than 48 h, Sun and Earth both up at touchdown. Same rule as the app's Window Finder; a day counts if any landing hour that UTC day works.

- Period searched: 2026-11-14 to 2027-11-13 (365 days).
- **Days that work: 32 of 365** (473 landing hours), in 13 clusters.
- Longest cluster: 3 days. Longest gap between clusters: 28 days.

| Cluster | First day | Last day | Days |
|--------:|-----------|----------|-----:|
| 1 | 2026-11-17 | 2026-11-19 | 3 |
| 2 | 2026-12-17 | 2026-12-19 | 3 |
| 3 | 2027-01-15 | 2027-01-17 | 3 |

## 5. Where to land: NASA's Artemis III limits on every 120 m square within 6 deg of the pole

- Ground tested: 104,184 km2. **Passing every hard limit: 14,928 km2, 14.3 %.**
- Share of the ground failing each limit (they overlap): sunlight 55.6 %, Earth in view 49.3 %, landing slope 45.7 %, walkable ground 5.5 %.
- **5,297 Goldilocks zones**; 643 are 1 km2 or larger; our model confirms a 6.5-day window with Sun and Earth for 4,224.
- Artemis check: 6 of the 9 candidate points pass every limit; 8 of the 9 have a passing zone within 12.5 km; 1 of our top 20 zones is near one. Ground near the points is 3.3 % of the area and 5.9 % of the passing ground.
- Radio delay Moon to Earth: 1.19 to 1.36 s one way, the same from every site.

## 7. Past landings

- Lunar soft-landing attempts in missions.csv, 1965 to 2025: **41** (24 landed, 4 tipped over, 11 crashed, 2 lost before landing).
- IM-1 Odysseus: slope 14.3 deg across 120 m, sunlight 36 %, Earth in view 100 %, passes every hard limit: no; IM-2 Athena: slope 3.6 deg across 120 m, sunlight 47 %, Earth in view 93 %, passes every hard limit: yes.
